newsitem.title: USA: LTV to close plant, sees $150 million charge.
newsitem.headline: LTV to close plant, sees $150 million charge.

text.p: LTV Steel said Monday it plans to close its Pittsburgh coke and by-products plant permanently by the end of 1997, resulting in a third-quarter charge of about $150 million.
The steelmaker said two-thirds of the plant's 750 employees will be eligible for retirement, while the rest will be considered to fill vacancies at other LTV plants.
The Cleveland-based company said it would have cost $400 million to $500 million to correct the plant's operating and environmental problems, which was prohibitive.
The coke plant is one of the country's oldest plants still in operation, producing coke for LTV Steel's blast furnaces in Cleveland and East Chicago, Ind.

J. James Murray, general manager of raw materials and coke operations, said the plant has reached the end of its working life, with operating and environmental performance having deteriorated. On March 6, the Environmental Protection Agency issued a notice of violation for emissions at the plant, he said.

"It would make no sense to perform major construction, which would involve the installation of new equipment and major rehabilitation, to put a temporary fix on the current operating and environmental problems," Murray said.
LTV produces flat rolled steel and tubular steel products and is a major supplier to the transportation, appliance, electrical equipment and service centre industries.
LTV's stock edged down 6 cents to $14.06 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
